handback.t:
Note to the coordinator: this planning run had not handed back before your messages arrived, so whatever report you already hold came from another run. As you asked, this message contains only the consumer section. A short appendix at the end lists the facts I verified this run, so you can check them against the report you have.

## Consumer decision: who sends live traffic through the front-end

**What the data supports today:** `data/lifelong/sft.jsonl` has 203 rows. All of them are `source=agent_report` (one world), all from one session spanning 2026-10-04 to 10-05, in 125 ingestor clusters. 40 rows (30 clusters) are held out. No normalised instruction repeats, so an exact cache would have 0 hits on this data. Production is `mesh-llm:base`, which has no adapter.

**Common gate G0.** It applies to every rung of every risky option, and it fails closed:
- Splits are cluster-blocked: clusters from `sft_meta.cluster` are ordered by their first timestamp and split into TUNE, HELD and CONF thirds. These clusters play the role of seeds.
- Each split needs at least 30 rows, at least 3 clusters and at least 2 worlds (world = `source`: agent_report vs human prompt).
- The judge must reject at least 0.70 of decoys, using the same constant as `llm/evaluate.py:36`. The release binary must be newer than `src/frontend.rs` and `src/main.rs`.
- Thresholds are tuned on TUNE only.
- Holm correction runs over every (axis × world × split) test of the candidate, using cluster-bootstrap p-values (`llm/stats.py:27` plus a new `holm()`).
- Quality is measured as delta = (judge score − 1) on rows not forwarded, 0 on forwarded rows. Claiming no quality loss needs TOST within ±0.01 on that delta.
- KEEP requires that saved tokens are a Holm-significant gain in the same world on both HELD and CONF, and that no axis shows a Holm-significant loss.
- Every wrong-answer ceiling below is checked against the upper bound of the 95% cluster-bootstrap CI, not the point estimate.

### A) Safe options (usable today, default off, fail closed)

**S1. Shadow / observe-only.**
- **How it works:** A repo-scoped `UserPromptSubmit` hook goes in a new `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\.claude\settings.json` (the repo has no `.claude\` today). It never touches the global hook at `~/.claude/settings.json:993`. The hook command is `python -m llm hook --shadow`, with a 5 s timeout.
  - It only appends {ts, sha256, project, prompt text} to `llm/models/frontend_shadow.jsonl`.
  - It prints nothing and always exits 0. It must never exit 2, because exit 2 blocks the prompt.
  - Claude Code forwards the prompt unchanged.
  - A batch command, `python -m llm shadow-drain`, runs later. It computes signals, the local answer and the Rust decision, joins Claude's real answer from the ingestor, and has the judge grade it.
- **Who assembles context:** Python, offline only. Nothing is forwarded differently.
- **Touches:**
  - new `.claude/settings.json`
  - `llm/__main__.py:55` (add `hook` and `shadow-drain`)
  - `llm/frontend.py` (`ask_local` at :60-65; replace the -99 sentinel at :65 with None)
  - `rust_decide` at :33-41 (check the return code, add a timeout, fall back to forward)
- **Failure and blast radius:** Prompts get stored on local disk, which is a privacy concern but stays on the box. If the hook crashes, Claude Code shows a hook
[...]
tice that means local share × wrong rate ≲ 0.005.
    - The confidence gate must be live: no −99 sentinel, and the grid stays within [−1, −0.02] and min-sim [0.3, 0.7] (fixing `llm/frontend.py:128`).
  - **Canary 5% → 20% → on:**
    - Needs at least 100 audited canary rows and at least 10 clusters per world.
    - The wrong upper CI must be ≤ 0.05, with no Holm-significant loss.
  - **Training and data:**
    - A second world: human prompts from `~/.claude/projects` transcripts via the ingestor.
    - An LoRA adapter trained on TUNE-era clusters (`llm train`); about 1000 or more rows is my estimate.
    - Confidence calibrated on TUNE.
    - A judge reaching decoy-reject ≥ 0.70, either rubric v2 or a larger judge than qwen2.5-coder:7b.

**R2. Verbatim replay from a verified cache.**
- **How it works:** This is `decide → Cache` (`src/frontend.rs:79`). Python sets `cache_hit` only when all of these hold:
  - the exact normalised match is in a bank that is strictly earlier in time;
  - outcome is success;
  - judge_score ≥ 0.9;
  - the instruction maps to only one answer;
  - same project;
  - age within the TTL;
  - git HEAD is unchanged when the instruction touches code.
  It also fixes the "verified" claim at `src/frontend.rs:3` and the cache lookup at `llm/frontend.py:93,101`.
- **Failure and blast radius:** A stale answer about code state that has since changed gets replayed silently.
- **Ladder:**
  - **Shadow → canary:** at least 50 hits that pass verification, a hit rate of at least 2% of traffic (otherwise the gain axis cannot pass), and a stale-wrong upper CI ≤ 0.05.
  - **Canary → on:** at least 100 audited hits and a wrong upper CI ≤ 0.02.
  - **Data:** only repeat volume; no model training. The current repeat count is 0.

**R3. Tool route auto-executes calc / units / csp.**
- **How it works:**
  - `--query-vec` and `--tool-exemplars` (ROUTE3, encoded with MiniLM) are added to `FRONTEND_KEYS` at `src/main.rs:713`. They are loaded at `cmd_frontend` (:717-763) and call `KnnRouter::route_guarded` (`src/knnroute.rs:78`, tau 0.6, smin 0.4). An allowlist limits it to calc, units and csp. `--tool` and `--query-vec` together is a usage error.
  - The executors are `Calc::eval_str` (`src/tools.rs:712`), `Units` (:842) and `Csp::solve_str` (:1016), each checked with `Identity::check_strict` (:1142).
  - Python extracts the arguments; this is the hard part.
- **Failure and blast radius:** Wrong tool or wrong argument produces a confident wrong number. Per R88, this saves about nothing on agent traffic.
- **Ladder:**
  - **Shadow → canary:** at least 100 routed rows in the human world, a wrong-route-or-argument upper CI ≤ 0.02, and saved tokens Holm-significant in the human world.
  - **Canary → on:** at least 200 audited rows and an upper CI ≤ 0.01.
  - **Data:** labelled real human arithmetic and units prompts, plus a battery of extracted arguments.

**R4. Local model drafts, Claude edits or verifies.**
- **How it works:** The S2 or S3 consumer attaches the local draft as context. Claude still answers and is the final authority.
- **Failure and blast radius:** Claude anchors on a wrong draft, and input tokens go up.
- **Ladder:**
  - **Gate for each rung:** paired replay of the same prompt with and without the draft. The quality delta must pass TOST ±0.01 against plain forward. Output tokens or latency must show a Holm-significant drop. The anchoring-error upper CI (Claude repeating a wrong draft) must be ≤ 0.05.
  - **Shadow minimum:** at least 200 paired rows. This spends real API calls, so the budget needs your approval.

**R5. Per-skill local takeover.**
- **How it works:** R1 restricted to an allowlist of skills or cluster types, for example short git or shell questions.
- **Failure and blast radius:** Errors stay inside the allowlisted skill, but skill misclassification lets out-of-scope prompts through.
- **Ladder:**
  - Each skill passes R1's gates on its own: at least 30 rows and at least 3 clusters per skill and split, with Holm across all skills.
  - Canary only for skills where the wrong upper CI is ≤ 0.05.
  - **Data:** skill labels from the ingestor clusters.

A hook that substitutes answers (block plus reason) is rejected as a separate option. It is only a delivery channel for R1, R2 or R5, has worse UX and a wider blast radius, and may come only after that option is "on" through S2.

### Recommendation
- **Start with S1 (shadow).** It never changes an answer, adds no latency (the hook only enqueues), and builds the shadow volume and the second world that every risky gate needs. S2 serves as the manual and debugging path.
- **First risky candidate to train toward safety: R1, with R5 as the way to narrow it.** It is the only option with measurable value on the data we have (the replay put 85% of prompts in local scope), and the existing replay, judge and adapter pipeline already measures it. R2 has 0 repeats, so it cannot pass the gain axis. R3 has about zero value on agent traffic (R88). R4 spends real API calls just to evaluate.
- **What blocks every risky option today:**
  1. There is only one world (every row is agent_report), so the Iron rule requiring more than one world fails.
  2. Judge decoy-reject is 0.60, below 0.70, so no wrong-rate figure can be certified.
  3. Splits are too small: one session, 40 held-out rows, 20 report rows.

  The 0.235 run should be logged in RD-LOG as **REJECTED**. Besides the three blockers above, the confidence gate was effectively off (min-conf −99 combined with the −99 missing-logprob sentinel), and wrong-local 0.235 is above the 0.10 target.

  - `ask_local` (:65) returns −99.0 when logprobs are missing, which passes min-conf −99.
  - `_sim` (:71) treats min-sim 0 differently from Rust (`src/frontend.rs:85`, `min_sim <= 0` means in-distribution) and counts cache as local.
  - `loc` (:138) counts cache and tool as local; they should be reported separately.
- Retrieval returns ids only (`src/main.rs:758`).
- `target/release/neural-mesh.exe` is from 04:17 and `src/main.rs` from 04:41, so the binary is stale.

- Gate constants are `MIN_N, MIN_SESSIONS = 30, 3` (`llm/evaluate.py:22`) and `MIN_DECOY_REJECT = 0.7` (:36).
